tasks.title: List Copilot model ids and the account plan
tasks.goal: Give the operator one CLI command that exposes the exact Copilot model ids, picker filtering, account policies, and Copilot plan returned by the two documented endpoints. This establishes the shared API client and the copilot-models/v1 document that later validation surfaces can reuse.

references.why: the two endpoints, required Copilot integration header, model fields, policy states, and plan response define this command's network contract
the --json document must embed its schema and all usage and failure paths must follow the repository's stdout, stderr, and exit-code conventions

acceptance: vloop models copilot reads the models endpoint and prints the plan line first, then picker-enabled models sorted by strings order; --all adds non-picker entries, and the policy column is enabled, disabled, or -.
vloop models copilot --json emits exactly one copilot-models/v1 document with plan null when unknown and policy null when the text column would be -.

The models and plan requests use the first non-empty token from COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, then gh auth token; the required Copilot integration header is sent, VLOOP_COPILOT_API_URL and VLOOP_GITHUB_API_URL replace only their respective bases, and no token reaches output or errors.

A missing login and a failed models request exit 1 with the brief's exact refusal; a missing or incorrect agent argument exits 2 with the brief's usage line. A failed or plan-less plan request is unknown, never an error.
The listing command uses a 20-second timeout per call and only the standard library; the vloop models command performs no network access for an invalid agent argument.
Committed Go tests exercise the output formats, filtering, JSON schema, request headers, unknown plan, failure, and no-login paths through httptest; no test reaches GitHub or Copilot for real.

tasks.title: Check Copilot model ids in config set
tasks.goal: Prevent a single model.<kind> write from introducing an unusable Copilot id while preserving config set's existing warning-only behavior for an unavailable API. The validation must use the pair configuration resolves to after a candidate write, including local and environment overrides.

references.why: C-1 requires checking the environment/local/shared/default value that will actually resolve after the write, and C-3 requires any defined JSON output to name its schema
the existing config set command owns --local, removal, warning placement, and exit-2 refusal behavior that this change must preserve
the existing Copilot login token lookup and secrecy rules are the token behavior config-set validation must reuse
it defines the all-models policy source used to distinguish missing, disabled, and policy-less ids

acceptance: Before writing model.<kind>, with or without --local, config set resolves agent.<kind> and the candidate model by C-1 and refuses a Copilot Claude alias, an id absent from the --all list, or a disabled id with the brief's exact exit-2 line; all other keys retain their existing validation.
The models request is skipped for a removed model, for a kind not resolved to copilot, and when the candidate is a Claude alias already decidable locally.

A failed, timed-out, or malformed models call and a missing login do not refuse a single-key set: it writes the value and emits exactly the brief's stderr warning with exit 0; the warning or error never contains the token.
Each config-set validation uses a five-second models-call timeout and writes nothing on refusal; a successful removal remains the existing remove operation and is never checked.
Committed Go tests use httptest and cover listed, absent, disabled, alias, unreachable, no-login, removal, --local, and environment/local precedence; no test reaches the real APIs.

tasks.title: Check configured Copilot models in doctor
tasks.goal: Extend doctor's existing Copilot preflight with one row that checks every in-use Copilot kind's resolved model and displays the account plan. This makes an edited invalid id refuse vloop run before a paid session starts without turning API unavailability into a refusal.

references.why: the copilot models row must follow the existing copilot row, reuse its login behavior and agent-in-use selection, and become part of the same run preflight result
C-1 requires each doctor's model and agent to be the resolved value, not a value read from only the shared file
the row uses the model policy and the separate account-plan endpoint under the documented five-second, warning-only failure contract

acceptance: When at least one session kind in use resolves to copilot, doctor places copilot models immediately after copilot and makes one models call and one plan call, reporting the distinct configured ids and plan exactly as the brief specifies in text and JSON.

An unlisted, disabled, or Claude-alias id produces a problem naming every affected model.<kind>, joined with ; ; a Claude alias is reported without any network request and receives ; ids not checked against the list when the list also cannot be reached.

A failed models call is a warning, an unknown or failed plan call remains plan unknown, and absence of login adds no models row because the existing copilot login row remains the problem; absence of a Copilot kind adds no models row or network call.
The row uses five-second timeouts, the token never appears in text or JSON, and the row's problem participates in vloop run's preflight so the run refuses before a plan session starts.

Committed Go tests use httptest for pass, missing, disabled, alias, unreachable, no-login, no-Copilot-kind, distinct-count, plan-unknown, ordering, and JSON-row behavior; no test reaches the real APIs.

tasks.title: Set several session kinds in one config command
tasks.goal: Replace up to fourteen separate config writes with one atomic --kinds operation for agent, model, and effort. Every candidate kind must be validated against its resolved pair before any shared or local file changes.

references.why: config set owns key validation, --local, empty-string removal, file editing, and refusal output; --kinds must preserve those semantics
C-1 makes the validation target the agent and model that resolve after all proposed writes, including environment and local overrides
it names the seven session kinds and the existing agent.<kind>, model.<kind>, and effort.<kind> key contract that --kinds may not expand

acceptance: vloop config set --kinds <comma-list> accepts exactly plan, gate-review, work, review, second-review, verify, and review-brief, requires at least one of --agent, --model, or --effort, and rejects a positional key or value with the brief's exact usage lines.
Every named kind's existing agent, model, and effort keys are validated as a single-key set would validate them; no new key or session kind is added.

All resulting Copilot pairs are checked before any write, one models request is made per invocation, removal is resolved by C-1, an environment override can still supply a Claude alias, and removing agent alone is never refused.

Any unknown kind, invalid value, alias, missing id, disabled id, or other refusal leaves both shared and local files byte-for-byte unchanged; --local targets only the local file and success prints only the warnings a single set would print.

Committed Go tests cover success, each option, every kind, exact usage errors, API reuse, model-result checks, removals, environment precedence, --local, and all-or-nothing failure; no test reaches a real API.

tasks.title: Document the Copilot model commands
tasks.goal: Replace the operator's manual API recipes with the supported vloop command and document how the new validation and multi-kind write affect configuration. Regenerate the command reference so the new command and flag are discoverable together.

references.why: the Copilot model ids section is the brief's named migration target and must retain the meaning of policy - and the new plan line
the generated command reference remains the authoritative cross-platform public CLI surface

acceptance: The Copilot model ids section uses vloop models copilot in place of the curl and PowerShell raw-API snippets, explains picker filtering, enabled/disabled/- policies, and the plan or plan unknown line.
The section states that config set and doctor validate ids for Copilot kinds and includes one vloop config set --kinds example; it contains no line that calls api.githubcopilot.com directly.
docs/guide/commands.md is regenerated from the completed CLI and includes vloop models copilot plus every --kinds, --agent, --model, and --effort surface.

tasks.title: Verify the Copilot model workflow end to end
tasks.goal: Run all earlier behavioral gates together and replay the brief's worked example in an initialized temporary repository. This closes the run only when listing, set-time checks, doctor, atomic --kinds writes, and failure warnings compose as one operator workflow.

references.why: the worked flow starts from the configuration keys documented here and must preserve the guide's resolution and --local semantics
the end-to-end oracle uses the public config set and config get surfaces whose existing validation and output the workflow must retain
the end-to-end oracle must observe doctor's public row and its use by the preflight without bypassing the existing copilot/login checks

acceptance: Every earlier task's planner-owned gate passes against the completed tree, and the close oracle executes the brief's worked example line by line with httptest servers and stub credentials in a temporary vloop-init repository.

The workflow proves exact picker and --all output, successful multi-kind writes, exit-2 absent/disabled/alias refusals, byte-for-byte all-or-nothing behavior, the doctor pass row, and warning-only writes and doctor after the stub stops.

No output, log, fixture, or error produced by the workflow contains the stub token, and the gate itself creates only temporary directories outside the repository; no network request reaches GitHub or Copilot.
